name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: SMW5 cable fault off Pakistan since 18 Nov
summary: A fault on the SMW5 cable off Pakistan since 18 Nov slows internet; GPS jamming hit Dutch flights on 16 Nov
state: A fault on the SMW5 submarine cable off Pakistan's coast caused slow speeds and outages from 18 Nov, with traffic rerouted and the cause not yet known (The National; Radio Pakistan, citing PTA, 19 Nov). No restoration announcement for this fault was found by 25 Nov; a separate SMW5 fault in July was repaired within a day. Suspected GPS jamming affected dozens of aircraft over the Netherlands on 16 Nov (Aviation24). A cable damage incident and GNSS interference keep Watch; no sabotage has been confirmed.
for_you: Little direct effect in the UK. Users and businesses in Pakistan may see slower international connections until the cable is repaired.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident (SMW5 off Pakistan, 18 Nov) and GNSS interference affecting aviation; no confirmed sabotage

sources.title: The National — Pakistan internet problems after subsea cable fault
Radio Pakistan — Submarine cable fault may affect internet services in Pakistan: PTA
Aviation24 — Dozens of aircraft affected by suspected GPS jamming over the Netherlands

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
